examples.en: The company forces overtime.
My parents don't force me to study.
No one can force you to attend.
Complaints came up after the rule was imposed.
I dislike an atmosphere where everyone is forced to attend.

examples.ko: 법으로 마스크 착용을 강제한 적이 있어요.
examples.en: At one time, wearing masks was made mandatory by law.

explain: '강제하다'는 싫어도 하게 만든다는 뜻이라 느낌이 강해요. 일상에서는 '억지로 시키다'나 '시키다'를 더 많이 써요. '강제'는 법이나 규칙처럼 힘이 있는 쪽이 할 때 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: Don't force your friend to drink.
phrases.nuance_ko: '강제하다'와 비슷하지만 사람에게 억지로 하게 할 때 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '강제하다', but used more in daily life when pushing a person to do something.

phrases.en: If you make someone do it against their will, they want to do it even less.
phrases.nuance_ko: 싫은데 하게 만든다는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Strongly suggests making someone do what they dislike.
phrases.en_equiv: to force someone against their will

phrases.en: This school doesn't require uniforms.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙으로 억지로 하게 하지 않는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it doesn't force people through rules.

explain_en: 강제하다 means making someone do something even if they don't want to, so it sounds strong. In daily talk people use 억지로 시키다 or 시키다 more. 강제 fits when a side with power, like a law or a rule, does it.

examples.en: It is important to follow public etiquette.

examples.ko: 지하철에서 큰 소리로 통화하면 공중도덕에 어긋나요.
examples.en: Talking loudly on the phone on the subway goes against public manners.

examples.ko: 공중도덕은 모두가 편하게 지내기 위한 약속이에요.
examples.en: Public etiquette is an agreement so that everyone can be comfortable.

examples.ko: 공중도덕이 없는 사람 때문에 화가 났어요.
examples.en: I got angry because of someone with no manners in public.
Standing in line is also part of public etiquette.

examples.ko: 우리 동네는 공중도덕 캠페인을 자주 해요.
examples.en: Our neighborhood often runs public etiquette campaigns.

explain: '공중도덕을 지키다'가 가장 자주 나오는 표현이에요. 반대로 안 지키는 사람에게는 '매너가 없다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: When everyone follows public etiquette, it's comfortable for all.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 기본이 되는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic collocation.

phrases.en: If you break public etiquette, other people are uncomfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙을 지키지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone doesn't follow the rules.

phrases.example: 큰 소리로 통화하는 사람은 매너가 없어요.
phrases.en: People who talk loudly on the phone have no manners.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 더 편하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more casual way to say it in daily conversation.

explain_en: '공중도덕을 지키다' (to follow public etiquette) is the most common phrase. For someone who doesn't, people also say '매너가 없다' (has no manners).

examples.ko: 이 휴대폰은 너무 구식이라 앱이 안 돼요.
examples.en: This phone is so outdated that apps do not work.
My grandmother's house has an old-style TV.
It is an old-style building, but the atmosphere is nice.

examples.ko: 그 생각은 요즘 보면 좀 구식이에요.
examples.en: That idea looks a bit old-fashioned these days.
My father still uses an old-style camera.

examples.ko: 구식 방법으로 만든 빵이라 더 맛있어요.
examples.en: The bread is made the old-fashioned way, so it tastes better.

explain: 반대말은 '신식'이에요. 기계나 방법이 오래돼서 요즘과 다를 때 쓰고, 사람에게 쓰면 생각이 낡았다는 느낌이라 실례가 될 수 있어요. '낡다'는 물건이 닳았다는 뜻이라 달라요.

phrases.en: They still use old-fashioned machines at the factory.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구식' 뒤에 물건 이름을 붙여 오래된 모델이나 형태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put an object after '구식' to describe an old model or type.

phrases.example: 이 방법은 구식이라서 시간이 오래 걸려요.
phrases.en: This method is outdated, so it takes a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래돼서 불편한 이유를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to give outdated-ness as the reason for an inconvenience.

phrases.example: 구식 방법으로는 숙제를 빨리 끝낼 수 없어요.
phrases.en: You can't finish the homework quickly with the old-fashioned method.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계뿐 아니라 일하는 방식에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It applies to ways of doing things, not only to machines.

explain_en: The opposite is '신식'. It is used for machines or methods that are old and different from today's. Applied to a person it implies outdated thinking and can be rude. '낡다' is different, meaning something is worn out.

examples.en: Don't say such nonsense.
Don't fight with your friend over such a trivial thing.
Where are you going wearing clothes like that?
I won't fall for a lie like that.
With an attitude like that, it's hard to get a job.

examples.ko: 그따위 걱정은 하지 말고 푹 자요.
examples.en: Stop worrying about such things and get some sleep.

explain: 상대의 말이나 물건을 낮춰 보고 못마땅하게 말하는 표현이라서 윗사람이나 처음 만난 사람에게는 쓰지 않아요. 가까운 사이에서도 화난 느낌이 나요. 가까운 것은 '이따위', 먼 것은 '저따위'예요.

phrases.en: Don't say such nonsense.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대의 말을 못마땅하게 여길 때 쓰는 거친 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A harsh phrase for disapproving of what someone said.

phrases.en: Why do you do your work like that?
phrases.nuance_ko: 행동 방식을 낮춰 보며 나무랄 때 써요. 화난 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to scold someone's way of doing things, with an angry tone.

phrases.en: I don't need this kind of junk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가까이 있는 것을 낮춰 말할 때 '그따위' 대신 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in place of 그따위 for something near the speaker.

explain_en: It looks down on what the other person said or has and expresses disapproval, so you don't use it with elders or people you've just met. Even among close friends it sounds angry. A closer thing is '이따위' and a farther one is '저따위'.

en: to be no more than that; to be enough

examples.en: If you fail, you can just try again, and that's all.
The scenery here is the best, so I come often.
It wouldn't have mattered if he didn't come, but I waited.
On a hot day, cold noodles are just perfect.

examples.ko: 싫으면 안 가도 그만인데 왜 고민해요?
examples.en: If you don't like it, you can just skip it, so why worry?

examples.ko: 나만 괜찮으면 그만이라고 생각하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't think it's fine as long as it's fine for you.

explain: 두 가지로 써요. '~(으)면 그만이다'는 그걸로 끝이고 더 신경 쓸 게 없다는 뜻이고, '경치가 그만이다'는 아주 좋다는 뜻이에요. '그만두다'와 헷갈리지 말고, 앞의 쓰임은 무심하게 들릴 수 있어요.

phrases.en: If you don't want to eat, you just don't eat. That's all.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~(으)면 그만이다'는 그걸로 끝이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '~(으)면 그만이다' means that's the end of it.

phrases.en: The cold noodles at this place taste great.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식 맛이 아주 좋다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise food as excellent.

phrases.en: The weather is perfect for a picnic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일을 하기에 아주 알맞게 좋다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it is just right for doing something.

explain_en: It has two uses: '~(으)면 그만이다' means that's all and nothing more needs worrying about, and '경치가 그만이다' means something is excellent. Don't confuse it with '그만두다' (to quit), and the first use can sound careless.

examples.en: There is a rumor that the owner ran the shop into the ground.

examples.ko: 형이 아버지 가게를 말아먹고 지금은 다른 일을 해요.
examples.en: My older brother ruined our dad's shop and now does a different job.

examples.ko: 한 번의 실수로 프로젝트를 말아먹을까 봐 걱정돼요.
examples.en: I'm worried that one mistake will wreck the project.

examples.ko: 시험을 말아먹어서 오늘은 기분이 안 좋아요.
examples.en: I totally bombed the exam, so I'm in a bad mood today.

examples.ko: 이번 발표를 말아먹으면 안 되니까 연습을 더 할게요.
examples.en: I can't mess up this presentation, so I'll practice more.
My friend regretted having squandered the inheritance.

explain: 사업, 시험, 일, 재산이 내 잘못으로 완전히 망했을 때 써요. 친한 사이의 구어체이고 조금 거친 느낌이라서 윗사람이나 격식 있는 자리에서는 '망치다', '실패하다'가 나아요. '국에 밥을 말아 먹다'는 띄어 쓰는 전혀 다른 표현이에요.

phrases.en: I blew yesterday's exam and I'm upset.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구 사이에서 시험을 크게 망쳤을 때 쓰는 구어체 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Casual speech among friends for completely botching an exam.

phrases.en: I heard he ruined his business and was left with only debt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사업을 잘못해서 완전히 망했다는 뜻이에요. 거친 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means a business failed completely because of someone's mistakes; it sounds rough.
phrases.en_equiv: run a business into the ground

phrases.en: I ruined my presentation, so I feel bad.
phrases.nuance_ko: '말아먹다'보다 덜 거칠어서 윗사람 앞에서도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less rough than 말아먹다, so it can be used with superiors.

explain_en: It is used when a business, exam, job or fortune is completely ruined through your own fault. It is casual and a bit rough, so with elders or in formal settings '망치다' or '실패하다' is better. '국에 밥을 말아 먹다' (to eat rice mixed into soup) is a completely different, spaced expression.

examples.ko: 요즘 복고 유행으로 옛날 노래가 다시 인기예요.
examples.en: With the current retro trend, old songs are popular again.
Retro-style clothes suit you well.
We decorated the cafe with a retro atmosphere.

examples.ko: 복고풍 노래를 들으면 어릴 때가 생각나요.
examples.en: Listening to retro-style songs reminds me of my childhood.

examples.ko: 복고 열풍 덕분에 LP를 사는 사람이 늘었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the retro craze, more people are buying LPs.
This drama is full of retro sentiment.

explain: 패션·음악·인테리어에서 옛 스타일을 다시 즐기는 유행을 말할 때 많이 써요. '복고풍', '복고 열풍', '복고 감성'처럼 붙여 쓰고, 외래어로는 '레트로'라고도 해요. 정치나 제도를 옛날로 되돌린다는 뜻으로도 쓰지만 일상에서는 유행 이야기가 더 흔해요.

phrases.en: Retro-style cafes are popular these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛날 느낌의 스타일을 말하고, 뒤에 명사를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to an old-fashioned style and goes before a noun.

phrases.example: 옛날 노래를 찾는 복고 열풍이 불고 있어요.
phrases.en: A retro craze for old songs is sweeping in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛 스타일이 크게 유행할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an old style becomes hugely popular.

phrases.en: I bought a retro-style bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: '복고'와 같은 뜻의 외래어로 젊은 사람들이 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A loanword meaning the same as 복고, popular among young people.

explain_en: It is commonly used for the trend of enjoying old styles again in fashion, music and interior design. It combines as '복고풍', '복고 열풍' and '복고 감성', and the loanword '레트로' is also used. It can also mean returning politics or systems to the past, but in daily life the trend meaning is more common.

examples.en: My older brother is a good role model for me.
A teacher has to set an example for students.
Look at the sample and write the same way.
I'll take this as a lesson and be careful.
Read the sample sentence first.

examples.ko: 본보기는 눈에 잘 띄는 곳에 붙여 두세요.
examples.en: Put the sample somewhere easy to see.

explain: '모범'은 따라 해도 좋은 모습이고, '본보기'는 따라 할 대상뿐 아니라 일부러 보여 주는 견본에도 써서 범위가 더 넓어요. 나쁜 일을 한 사람을 '본보기로 벌주다'처럼 경고용으로도 써요.

phrases.example: 저는 언니를 본보기로 삼아서 열심히 공부해요.
phrases.en: I take my older sister as a model and study hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 따라 하고 싶은 사람이나 일을 기준으로 정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you pick someone or something as a model to follow.

phrases.en: The senior became a good example for the juniors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람이 따라 할 만한 모습을 보여 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone's behavior is worth others following.

phrases.example: 선생님은 규칙을 어긴 학생을 본보기로 혼냈어요.
phrases.en: The teacher scolded the student who broke the rules as an example to others.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람들이 보고 조심하도록 일부러 벌줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when punishing someone on purpose as a warning to others.
phrases.en_equiv: to scold as a warning example

explain_en: 모범 is a good model worth following, while 본보기 is wider: it can also be a sample shown on purpose. It is even used for warning, as in '본보기로 벌주다' (punish as an example to others).

examples.ko: 아날로그 시계는 바늘로 시간을 보여 줘요.
examples.en: An analog clock shows the time with hands.
Analog things have been catching the eye again lately.

examples.ko: 저는 종이 일기장 같은 아날로그를 좋아해요.
examples.en: I like analog things, like a paper diary.
Music feels different when you listen to it in analog.
Please explain the difference between digital and analog.
My father uses an analog-style camera.

explain: 보통 '디지털'과 짝으로 써요. '아날로그 감성'은 손으로 만지는 옛날 물건의 따뜻한 느낌을 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.en: I like the analog feeling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손으로 만지는 옛날 물건의 따뜻한 느낌을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the warm feeling of old things you handle by hand.

phrases.example: 이 가게는 아직 아날로그 방식으로 일해요.
phrases.en: This shop still works in an analog way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 컴퓨터를 쓰지 않는 옛날 방식을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the old way of doing things without computers.

phrases.en: Digital and analog are different from each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 말을 짝으로 나란히 쓰는 가장 흔한 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing of the two words.

explain_en: It is usually paired with 'digital'. 'Analog gamseong' (analog sensibility) is used for the warm feel of old, hands-on things.

examples.ko: 오래된 인습 때문에 여자아이가 학교에 못 가던 시절이 있었어요.
examples.en: There was a time when girls couldn't go to school because of old customs.
We need new attempts that break from convention.

examples.ko: 마을에는 아직도 낡은 인습이 남아 있어요.
examples.en: Outdated customs still remain in the village.

examples.ko: 인습에 얽매이지 않는 사람이 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to be a person not bound by convention.

examples.ko: 그 소설은 그 시대의 인습을 비판해요.
examples.en: That novel criticizes the conventions of its time.
Wrong customs must be corrected as soon as possible.

explain: '관습'은 중립적인 말이지만 '인습'은 오래 이어졌어도 낡고 나쁘다는 평가가 들어 있어요. '인습을 깨다/타파하다', '인습에 얽매이다'로 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 그 감독은 영화계의 인습을 깨고 새로운 방식을 시도했어요.
phrases.en: The director broke the film world's old customs and tried a new approach.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낡은 관행을 바꾼다는 뜻으로 가장 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to say breaking away from outdated customs.

phrases.example: 인습에 얽매이면 새로운 생각을 하기 어려워요.
phrases.en: If you are bound by old customs, it is hard to think in new ways.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낡은 관습에서 벗어나지 못하는 상태를 비판적으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes, critically, being unable to get free of old customs.

phrases.example: 낡은 인습 때문에 불편을 겪는 사람이 많아요.
phrases.en: Many people suffer inconvenience because of outdated customs.
phrases.nuance_ko: '낡은'을 붙여 인습이 나쁘다는 평가를 더 분명히 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 낡은 makes the negative judgment of the custom even clearer.

explain_en: '관습' is neutral, but '인습' carries a judgment that the custom is old and bad even though it lasted long. Common uses are '인습을 깨다/타파하다' and '인습에 얽매이다'.

en: to buy; to get; to prepare

examples.en: I bought a new refrigerator before moving.
If you want to marry, you must get a home first.
My mother is preparing the holiday food.

examples.ko: 차를 장만하는 데 돈이 많이 들어요.
examples.en: It costs a lot to get a car.
It's convenient to get winter clothes ahead of time.
I'll get a desk this month.

explain: '사다'는 그냥 물건을 사는 것이고, '장만하다'는 필요해서 미리 갖추는 느낌이에요. 집, 차, 가구처럼 크거나 꼭 필요한 것에 잘 써요. 명절 음식을 '준비하다'라는 뜻으로도 써요.

phrases.en: I worked hard and finally bought a house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 돈이 드는 집이나 차를 갖출 때 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits well with big purchases like a house or a car.

phrases.en: For the holiday, we prepare food for the family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 '준비하다'라는 뜻으로 쓸 때도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can also mean to prepare food.

phrases.en: I saved money and got a car.
phrases.nuance_ko: '장만하다'와 비슷하게 필요한 것을 갖출 때 써요. 돈이나 방법에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 장만하다 for getting what you need. Also used for money or ways to do something.

explain_en: 사다 simply means to buy; 장만하다 carries the feeling of getting something you need and having it ready. It fits big or essential things such as a house, a car, or furniture. It can also mean preparing food for a holiday.

dis.h: acquire or prepare something needed, often big

p.n: 사다 states the purchase only; 장만하다 stresses getting it ready for a purpose.
